global_summary: This video documents the multi-stage process of installing and monitoring a Vertical Log Hive (a natural bee hive) in a backyard tree. It begins with the hive's setup and inoculation, followed by a wild swarm moving in on April 4, 2013. The narrative then follows periodic 'openings' of the hive over weeks and months (e.g., 6 days, 17 days, 37 days, and 11 weeks after the swarm's arrival) to inspect the colony's growth. Viewers see the bees building comb, forming dense clusters, and thriving within the tree cavity. The beekeeper interacts with the hive by opening secured panels, inspecting the comb, and handling the bees—all performed without smoke, as noted in the final title card 'Gaia Bees.' The video serves as an observational tutorial on natural beekeeping and hive establishment.
